name: Gibraltar
region: Southern Europe (Iberian peninsula), British Overseas Territory, outside the EU
summary: No capital gains tax (except, from 2025, property dealing by owners of five or more taxable properties), no tax on interest, no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. An ordinarily resident individual is taxed on foreign employment and self-employment income and on 'other income' (Income Tax Act 2010 s. 11(2), Sch. 1 Tables B and C), but dividends from companies listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, or paid out of profits on which Gibraltar charged no tax, are excluded from the charge (Table C Class 1(a)(iii)-(iv)), so a portfolio of foreign shares produces no Gibraltar tax for a resident. Income tax (up to 39% / 28%) bites mainly on Gibraltar-source and employment income. Category 2 (high-net-worth) status excludes foreign dividends from assessable income (Rule 10(1)), caps assessable income at GBP 118,000 and charges a minimum tax of GBP 37,000 a year; one certificate can cover spouse and children (Rule 11). From June 2026 new applicants need GBP 5 million net assets (was GBP 2 million).

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: Income tax on income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar, plus certain foreign income for ordinarily resident individuals; two systems (Allowances Based: top rate 39%; Gross Income Based: top rate 25-28%), taxpayer pays the lower. No tax on capital gains or interest.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days in a tax year, or more than 300 days in aggregate over three consecutive tax years. Requires a Gibraltar residence permit or Category 2 certificate.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains. Exception from 1 Jan 2025: profits on selling Gibraltar property (and shares in property-holding entities) are taxable if the person holds, directly or indirectly, five or more taxable properties (or did so over five consecutive periods); primary residence and estate disposals excluded. The Income Tax Act 2010 has no charge on capital gains: Schedule 1 charges only the heads in Tables A to C and, from 1 Jan 2025, profits from residential property disposals (Part 2).

capital_gains.rate_basis: No CGT. real_estate_local 0 assumes fewer than five taxable Gibraltar properties.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading as a business (in Gibraltar) could be taxable trading income; not researched.

dividends.summary: Under s. 11(2) of the Income Tax Act 2010 an ordinarily resident individual is chargeable on Table B and Table C income arising or received outside Gibraltar. Table C Class 1(a) charges dividends except those paid (i) by a company to another company, (ii) to a person not ordinarily resident, (iii) by a company whose shares are listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, or (iv) out of profits or gains on which no tax has been charged under the Act, to the extent of those profits. Dividends from foreign listed companies, and from foreign companies whose profits Gibraltar never charged, are therefore untaxed. Income from funds marketed to the public is not charged (Class 2(a)); interest is not a head of charge. Dividends from unlisted Gibraltar companies are taxed to the extent of taxable underlying profits, with a tax credit.

open_questions: The Gazette notice designating Recognised Stock Exchanges (Income Tax Act 2010 interpretation section and Sch. 1 Table C Class 1(a)) was not found; limb (iv) covers dividends out of profits not charged to Gibraltar tax in any case.
dividends.rate_basis: Foreign listed shares: Table C Class 1(a)(iii) and (iv) of Schedule 1 exclude the dividend from the charge, so 0. Gibraltar company dividends: taxed at personal rates (up to 39%) to the extent of taxable underlying profits, with a tax credit; domestic_rate left null. Domestic rate 0: the family's 'domestic' share of the portfolio is taken as shares listed on a Recognised Stock Exchange, whose dividends are outside assessable income under the same Table C Class 1(a)(iii); Gibraltar has almost no listed companies of its own.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends (general knowledge, not verified).
dividends.treaty_network: Essentially no comprehensive double tax treaties (UK-Gibraltar treaty signed 2019 only); full non-treaty WHT on foreign dividends (not verified).
dividends.important_exceptions: The Commissioner designates Recognised Stock Exchanges by Gazette notice; the notice was not found, so listing on a given exchange is not confirmed (limb (iv) would still exempt dividends from foreign profits that Gibraltar did not tax). Dividends from private foreign companies or from non-public funds follow the entity rules.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: General rates (municipal property rates) apply; not researched.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax, no estate duty and no gift tax. Stamp duty applies to transfers of Gibraltar real estate and shares in companies owning it (up to 4.5% on the excess over GBP 800,000), mainly on sales.
open_questions: Whether stamp duty applies to an inheritance or gift of Gibraltar property to a child not confirmed.

regimes.name: Category 2 high-net-worth individual
regimes.description: Assessable income is capped at GBP 118,000 a year (Rule 9(4)(a)) and charged only under the Allowances Based System (Rule 9(3), 9(5)); minimum tax GBP 37,000 a year (Rule 9(4)(b)); maximum tax GBP 42,380 at current rates (Income Tax Office). Dividends, pensions and emoluments from outside Gibraltar are not taken into account (Rule 10(1)); Gibraltar rents and permitted Gibraltar business or employment income are assessable (Rule 10(3)-(4)). For a passive foreign portfolio the tax is therefore the GBP 37,000 minimum: the regime buys a residence route and certainty, not a saving over ordinary residence, where the same portfolio is untaxed.
regimes.eligibility: Not present in Gibraltar more than 183 days in any of the last five years or on average 90 days in any three, and no trade, business or employment there in that period (Rule 4); approved residential accommodation in Gibraltar for exclusive use for the whole year (Rule 3); the Finance Centre Director must be satisfied of substantial and sound financial standing and good character (Rule 6). Net assets of GBP 5 million for new applicants from June 2026 (GBP 2 million before): announced by the government on 18 June 2026; the Rules themselves set no figure, and existing holders are grandfathered.

lump_sum.notes: Minimum tax GBP 37,000 for every year after the year of application (Rule 9(4)(b); GBP 3,083.33 a month in the first and last year, 9(4)(c)-(d)). The tax is the greater of the minimum and the Allowances Based tax on the first GBP 118,000 of assessable income, which is GBP 42,380 at the cap (Income Tax Office). Foreign dividends, pensions and emoluments are outside assessable income unless the holder elects to include them (Rule 10(1)-(2)); capital gains are not taxed in Gibraltar. Gibraltar rents and permitted Gibraltar work are assessable on top (Rule 10(3)-(5)); the lump_sum 'covers' list therefore no longer includes domestic income (earlier version of this file did). A spouse and children can be treated as part of the holder's income by an election (Rule 11(1)), or apply for their own certificate (Rule 11(5)), so one certificate and one minimum can cover the family. An advance payment equal to the maximum tax under Rule 9(4)(a) is due by 30 November and is refundable on surrender (Rule 8); the application fee is GBP 1,233, rising to GBP 5,000 (press release 469/2026). Not indexed by law: amounts changed only by Legal Notice (last LN 2022/173).

regimes.duration_note: The certificate is effective for an indefinite period (Rule 6) while the holder keeps meeting the conditions of Rules 3, 5 and 7 (accommodation, good standing, taxes and the minimum paid) and submits it for endorsement every three years (Rule 7(3)). It lapses if the holder declares no Gibraltar tax liability (Rule 7(4)).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present in Gibraltar 183 days or more in a tax year, or more than 300 days in aggregate over three consecutive years of assessment.

routes.name: Category 2 certificate
routes.requirements: Net assets GBP 5 million for applications from June 2026 (GBP 2 million before; announced 18 June 2026, existing holders grandfathered), approved accommodation for exclusive use, no presence over 183 days in any of the previous five years and no Gibraltar business or employment (Rules 3-4). Spouse and children can be covered by one election (Rule 11).

corporate.summary: Territorial corporate tax on income accrued in or derived from Gibraltar; rate not verified in this research.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent from a listing-portal sample (asking rents). Property stamp duty: 0% up to GBP 200,000; above GBP 800,000: 3% on first 350,000, 3.5% on next 450,000, 4.5% on balance. Purchase price, health insurance and housekeeper costs not sourced.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 13 residential lettings with 4+ bedrooms on PropertyGibraltar.com on 2026-10-15 (14 listed; one at GBP 895, evidently a room let, excluded). Range GBP 3,350-14,000; South District and Westside villas GBP 6,700-14,000. Large family houses are scarce; most are apartments. Asking rents in GBP (GIP at par). Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed on worldwide income; Gibraltar adds little. No US-Gibraltar income tax treaty (not verified).
open_questions: The Gazette notice designating Recognised Stock Exchanges was not found; the foreign-dividend exclusion rests also on limb (iv) (profits not charged to Gibraltar tax).
Corporate tax rate, treaty network and post-Brexit residence rules for EU nationals not verified.

Category 2 net-assets requirement: GBP 5 million is government policy announced 18 June 2026 (existing holders grandfathered); the Rules contain no figure, and the Finance Centre page was not updated when checked by other sources.
Category 2 first-year advance payment (maximum tax under Rule 9(4)(a)) and the application fee (GBP 1,233, to rise to GBP 5,000) are one-off and not in the lump_sum amount.
